name: Floors ran → gate the attempt (check_gate: advance / retry / escalate)
description:
The gate station (design SB4, group 7D). After check_floors has recorded the structural findings, gate the task's attempt: force check_gate, which reads the recorded measurement.result.<i>.passed + floor.finding.<i>.rejected + the DISTINCT count of task.attempt.<i> against task.spec.<i>.budget and DERIVES the route — advance (measured green, no floor rejected), retry (not clean, budget remains), or escalate (not clean, budget exhausted, OR a required fact missing → fail closed). Three router rules (dev-from-task/08a/b/c) act on the decision. This is a TOOL, not a rule condition, because a rule firing on a LOOP entity cannot read RUN facts, distinct-object budget counting is not a length_* operator, and a scalar field-to-field compare floods the semstreams #519 WARN — all three force the comparison into Go (the architect's 7D ruling). G3: check_gate takes only task_index; the route is harness-derived, never a model claim.

TRIGGER = the FLOORS loop terminal, chained on a loop marker (not a run fact — a run-fact trigger would need a field-to-field self-extinguish guard, which floods #519). check_floors stamps dev.floors_done on ITS OWN loop once it records the findings (like measure_task stamps dev.measure_done → the floors station). This rule fires on that marker: agent.loop.role=coordinator (the floors loop is a coordinator loop scoped to check_floors) AND dev.floors_done ne "". The pair distinguishes the floors loop from the OTHER coordinator loops that also reach outcome=success (provision/measure/create_change/validate/project_tasks) — none carry dev.floors_done. No outcome=success gate is needed (the marker is stamped only on check_floors' success path). It is stamped for a REJECTING floors run too, so a fabrication finding still chains to the gate (which decides retry); only a check_floors ERROR (no marker) stalls the chain toward the human.

RUN BINDING: run_scope=inherit reads the floors loop's bare agent.run and binds the check_gate loop's RunID to the same run, so check_gate reads THIS run's measurement/floor/budget facts and stamps dev.gate.<i>.* on the run.

ROLE = coordinator (design roster: only Sarah/Amelia/Quinn; Sarah owns the harness tools). tool_choice=function forces check_gate and tools stays nil (global discovery); the loop calls it and StopLoops, writing dev.gate.* + the dev.gate_decision loop marker (not coordinator.decision.*), so it triggers no coordinator decision rule.

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps the fired-once marker dev.gate_dispatched=$entity.instance on the floors loop (the firing entity), and the dev.gate_dispatched length_eq 0 guard makes the trigger flip false the moment it fires. House restart-safety pattern (dev-from-task/04..06): publish_agent is NOT idempotent and dev.floors_done stays stamped, so WITHOUT this marker a graph replay with RULE_STATE lost would re-spawn a DUPLICATE gate loop. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish so a publish failure stalls-toward-human rather than duplicating. LOOP-scoped (like dev.dispatched) because this rule fires on the floors loop. A fresh floors loop per attempt carries no dev.gate_dispatched, so the gate re-runs per attempt for free.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt: SEMDEV — the developed task was measured and the structural floors ran. Now gate the attempt: call check_gate with task_index 0. The harness reads the recorded measurement and floor findings and the attempt count against the task's iteration budget and derives advance / retry / escalate — you supply no verdict, count, or decision. Calling check_gate completes your turn.

metadata.station: check_gate — gate the attempt on the floors-loop terminal (SB4, 7D)
metadata.trigger_rationale: fires on the FLOORS loop terminal via the dev.floors_done loop marker (check_floors stamps it on its own loop, the measure→floors precedent). role=coordinator + dev.floors_done distinguishes the floors loop from the other coordinator loops that also reach success. Loop-marker chaining, NOT a run-fact field-to-field trigger, to stay warn-free (#519).
metadata.role_rationale: coordinator (Sarah owns the harness tools). tool_choice=function:check_gate + nil tools (global discovery) forces the call — a gating turn, not a routing turn. Mirrors dev-from-task/05 measure and /06 floors.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the LOOP-scoped dev.gate_dispatched marker + length_eq 0 guard (house pattern). publish_agent is not idempotent, so the one-shot is intrinsic; check_gate's StopLoop keeps the gate loop one turn. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish. A fresh floors loop per attempt re-arms the gate for free.
metadata.g3: check_gate takes only task_index; it reads harness-stamped facts (measurement/floors/budget/attempt count) and derives the route in Go, never a model claim.
metadata.chain_note: the three router rules (dev-from-task/08a/b/c) fire on the check_gate LOOP's dev.gate_decision marker (advance→dev.task_cleared, retry→re-dispatch developer, escalate→run.awaiting_human park), mutually exclusive on the single decision value (literal eq, #519-immune).
metadata.deferred_tool_scoping: tools omitted = global discovery; tool_choice=function:check_gate structurally constrains the call. Residual is populating bootstrap allowed_tools before the first real-LLM token (MEDIUM-3). Inert under the mock.
